title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 80
paragraphs: He answered as follows: “You advise very well, and the news you bring is good, since you have come having witnessed with your own eyes what I wished would come to pass. For you should know that what the Medes are doing was prompted by me, because when the Greeks would not come to battle of their own will, it was necessary to bring them to it against their will. But since you have come bearing good news, report it to them yourself. For if I speak of these things, I shall be thought to have invented them, and I shall not convince them, but they will believe that the barbarians are doing no such thing. Come forward yourself and tell them how matters stand; and when you have declared it, if they are persuaded, that will be best; but if they do not find it credible, it will make no difference as far as we are concerned, for they will no longer be able to flee — if, as you say, we are surrounded on all sides.”
